reviewMethod: Complete line-by-line semantic review of the root ignore, production environment, agent, lint, Next.js, PostCSS and TypeScript configuration authorities plus the permanent root-configuration policy, including effective Git ignore behavior, Docker build-context exposure, production placeholder validation, compiler strictness, CommonJS lint coverage, immutable build identity and security response headers.

residualRisks.statement: This bounded slice reviews eleven root-configuration authority files only; the remaining Batch 1 package, governance, deployment and script paths retain their pending status and no repository-wide completion claim is made.

Filename-based ignore controls cannot identify a secret stored under an arbitrary non-environment filename; the independent full-history and working-tree secret-scanning authorities remain mandatory defense in depth.
The production PM2 file is now linted and retains a focused startup-boundary test, but its complete operational semantics remain assigned to pending Batch 11 review.

reviewNotes: Every build-context exclusion and re-inclusion was reviewed against Dockerfile COPY behavior, repository-generated evidence locations, local agent state, environment files, private-key formats and large local artifacts.
Generated artifacts and local agent state are now excluded before Docker sends the context to the daemon or copies it into the builder.

findings.attackPath: Dockerfile copies the complete non-ignored context into the builder, while generated artifacts and root .agents state were Git-ignored but not Docker-ignored; local evidence, diagnostics or agent context could therefore be sent to the daemon and retained in a builder layer.
findings.affectedInvariant: Untracked local evidence and agent state must never enter a production build context.
findings.evidence: git check-ignore confirmed artifacts are local-only, Dockerfile line 20 uses COPY . ., and the former Docker ignore list contained neither artifacts nor .agents.
findings.verificationRequirement: The permanent root-configuration policy must require both exclusions and reject any effective re-inclusion.

reviewNotes: All public origins, distinct secret placeholders, proxy inputs, PostgreSQL/Redis authorities, rate-limit credentials, custody fail-closed flags and optional Mentor model settings were reviewed against validate-env and production-host supply-chain tests.
The unchanged template fails validation until every required placeholder is replaced, passes the governed replacement fixture and keeps real withdrawals and custody simulation disabled.
Dependency, test, Next.js, production, local artifact, debug, environment, Vercel, TypeScript and runtime-data patterns were reviewed with effective git check-ignore behavior.
Every .env variant is now ignored while inert .env.example and .env.*.example templates remain reviewable and committable.

findings.attackPath: The former explicit list ignored .env, .env.local, .env.production and .env.*.local but allowed common secret-bearing names such as .env.staging, .env.test and .env.development to appear as committable files.
findings.affectedInvariant: Every real environment file must be excluded from Git regardless of deployment stage naming.
findings.evidence: git check-ignore --no-index returned non-ignored for .env.staging, .env.test and .env.development before remediation; the broad rule plus explicit example re-inclusions now produces the intended result for all tested names.
findings.verificationRequirement: A permanent test must exercise effective Git ignore behavior for production, local, staging, test and development names and prove examples remain committable.

reviewNotes: The file is valid JSON and contains only the editor schema locator; it declares no executable command, MCP server, credential or repository mutation.

The only agent instruction directs contributors to the installed Next.js 16 documentation inside node_modules before code changes and contains no remote execution, credential access or authority override.
Claude delegates to the canonical AGENTS.md rather than maintaining a divergent instruction surface.
Next.js and TypeScript presets, zero-debt correctness rules, rule scope and every global ignore were reviewed against the permanent ESLint authority.
CommonJS files now receive their own Node-safe core-rule configuration, and the production PM2 configuration passes ESLint instead of relying on a broad config-file exclusion.

findings.attackPath: The former *.config.cjs global ignore silently excluded every present or future CommonJS configuration file from ESLint, including the production PM2 entry point.
findings.affectedInvariant: Executable repository configuration must not disappear from static analysis because of a broad filename class.
findings.evidence: ESLint reported ecosystem.config.cjs as ignored before remediation; the new CommonJS block supplies readonly Node globals and core no-undef/no-unused-vars rules, and both ecosystem.config.cjs and a future config path are now non-ignored.
findings.verificationRequirement: The root policy and ESLint API test must reject the broad ignore and prove both current and future CommonJS config paths remain lintable.

reviewNotes: Immutable build identity, strict React behavior, framework disclosure, Turbopack root and every response header were reviewed against proxy CSP and production build/runtime evidence.
Security headers remain global; DNS prefetch is now disabled so an unvisited external link does not trigger speculative name resolution.

findings.attackPath: X-DNS-Prefetch-Control was explicitly on, allowing browsers to resolve external link hostnames before a user chose to follow them and exposing avoidable browsing-context metadata.
findings.affectedInvariant: The financial application must not enable speculative third-party network disclosure without a demonstrated product requirement.
findings.evidence: The former header value was on; the remediated global header is off, matching the conservative OWASP header recommendation for uncontrolled links.
findings.verificationRequirement: The root policy mutation test must reject re-enabling DNS prefetch, and the production browser/header gate must pass on the exact head.

reviewNotes: The configuration exposes only the expected Tailwind PostCSS plugin and no dynamic loading, remote resource or environment-dependent mutation.

Input typing, exact ignore lines, complete environment re-inclusion rejection, CommonJS lint contract, browser headers, immutable build identity, parsed TypeScript/Kilo configuration and agent/tool delegation checks were reviewed.

The policy allows only the two inert example re-inclusions, rejects every other .env or .env.* negation regardless of future stage name, and is exercised by production-source acceptance, effective Git/ESLint behavior and negative mutations.

findings.attackPath: The former policy rejected explicit re-inclusion of only five named environment files, so a future rule such as !.env.preview could make a new secret-bearing file committable while the guard still passed.
findings.affectedInvariant: Only inert .env example templates may be re-included after the broad environment-file ignore.
findings.evidence: The former loop enumerated local, production, staging, test and development names; a mutation adding !.env.preview produced no policy finding.
findings.verificationRequirement: The root policy must inspect every .env-class negation, allow only the two governed example patterns and reject an arbitrary future stage name in a permanent mutation test.

reviewNotes: Target libraries, strict/no-emit compiler contract, bundler resolution, isolated modules, Next plugin, canonical source alias, generated Next type inputs and explicit exclusions were reviewed.
The permanent root policy parses the actual JSON and rejects weakening strict, noEmit, isolatedModules, bundler resolution, React JSX or the Next plugin.
